91
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, March 19, 2013/Phalguna 28, 1934 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Environment and Forests; Finance; Health and Family Welfare;
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Power)
Total number of questions — 20
Precautionary measures at Bombay
High
*301. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) the planned capacity augmentation
from Bombay High Oil Fields after
installation of a new platform in December,
2012 which is supposed to be the
replacement of such a facility destroyed in
a fire in the vicinity in July, 2007; and
(b) the details of precautionary
measures adopted so that a situation similar
to the Bombay High Oil Fields does not
recur in oil offshore platforms where a
Shipping Corporation supply vessel
became non-functional due to cyclonic
weather and hit the gas-pumping pipeline
of the old platform?
Regulatory legislation to check
surrogacy
*302. SHRIMATI JHARNA DAS
BAIDYA: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a regulatory legislation to
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
check surrogacy and related issues is being
formulated;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Fall in inflation
†*303. DR. YOGENDRA P. TRIVEDI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether fall in the rate of inflation
has been noticed during the last few
months;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor and the
details of steps Government will take to
control inflation?
Opening of more CGHS Wellness
Centres in NCR
*304. SHRI SHADI LAL BATRA: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any
proposal for opening of more CGHS
Wellness Centres in the National Capital
Region (NCR);

92
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) by when these Wellness Centres will
be made functional for the CGHS
beneficiaries, particularly in Haryana and
Uttar Pradesh?
Non-starting of manufacturing by
licensed drug companies
†*305. SHRI RASHEED MASOOD:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of such drug companies
which have not till date started
manufacturing of drugs even after getting
the requisite licences; and
(b) the details of the action taken against
such companies?
Levy of inspection charges by State
Governments on electrical
installations
*306. SHRI PARSHOTTAM
KHODABHAI RUPALA: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Electric
Regulatory Commission (CERC) is
examining and finalising the issue of
restoring the earlier practice of levy of
inspection charges by the State
Governments for testing and inspection of
electrical installations;
(b) if so, by when;
(c) whether the Central Government is
aware of the fact that due to discontinuation
of earlier practice of levying of inspection
charges, State Governments are suffering
revenue losses; and
(d) the number of State Governments
which have approached the Central
Government and the details of action taken
in this regard?
Multiple mortgaging of property by
builders
*307. SHRI PARVEZ HASHMI: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government is aware that a
number of builders in the National Capital
Region (NCR) have mortgaged the same
property twice and thrice to different banks
especially in public sector banks like
HUDCO, SBI, Corporation Bank etc. by
submitting fraudulent papers in connivance
with local bank authorities;
(b) whether maximum number of such
economical offences have been reported to
be committed by M/s Supertech and
M/s Assotech Ltd. in their townships at
metropolis, Rudrapur and in NCR; and
(c) if so, the details of action
Government proposes to influence banks
to avoid sanctioning of loans on properties
being sold by M/s Supertech?
Return on NPS Funds
*308. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
total return on New Pension Scheme (NPS)
Funds in respect of the Central
Government employees, so far, under
various fund managers like SBI, UTI and
LIC etc. has been only 50 to 60 per cent in
nine years;
(b) if so, the details thereof, fund-wise;
(c) whether total return on NPS Funds
in respect of the State Government
employees is also not satisfactory;

93
(d) if so, the details thereof since its
inception in 2004 and the reasons therefor;
and
(e) whether NPS Fund managers have
failed to achieve the desired and comfortable
growth?

Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
Bihar, a major State of the country, is facing

Disposal of effluents by distilleries
2326. DR. T. N. SEEMA: Will the
Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
the standards to be complied by distilleries
for disposal of treated effluents are not
being followed by several distilleries;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of surprise inspections
carried out by the Central and each of the
State Pollution Control Boards (PCBs) for
verification of compliance by distilleries to
the prescribed pollution control norms
during 2012 along with action taken reports;
(d) whether CPCB and State PCBs have
given a fixed time-frame to distilleries for
establishing facilities to achieve Zero Liquid
Discharge (ZLD);
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Ban on new industries in
Maharashtra
†2327. SHRI ISHWARLAL
SHANKARLAL JAIN:
SHRI ANIL DESAI:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government has
imposed a ban on setting up of new
industries in Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg
districts of the Konkan region of
Maharashtra;
(b) if so, whether the State Government
has requested or submitted a proposal for
lifting the ban on setting up of new
industries in these districts;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether this decision of the Central
Government is causing substantial
hindrances in the course of economic
development of these districts of the State;
(e) whether Government intends to lift
the ban imposed on the setting up of new
industries in these areas; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?

535
Reduction of contours of Kolleru lake
in Andhra Pradesh
2328. SHRIMATI T. RATNA BAI:
SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has objected
to the reduction of contours of Kolleru lake
in Andhra Pradesh from 5 to 3;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps being taken to amend the
wildlife acts for this purpose?
Counting of birds and animals
2329. SHRI RAMA CHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) the procedure adopted by the
department to identify the forest cover area
and how frequently the survey is
conducted and the latest figure;
(b) whether the counting of birds and
animals in the forest is accurate; and
(c) if so, the latest figure of species of
tigers, lions, elephants, leopards and birds
in India?
Relocation of the settlement areas in
National Parks in Assam
2330. SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken any
steps to relocate the settlement areas from
the various National Parks in Assam as the
presence of people inside the park is
contrary to the Rule and Regulations and it
is also affecting the wild life;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the details of the re-plantation
activities inside forest cover area?
Conservation of endangered species of
plants and animals in J&K
2331. SHRI G . N. RATANPURI: Will
the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether any study has been
conducted to identify endangered species
of plants and animals in Jammu and
Kashmir (J&K);
(b) whether unregulated tourism and
human interference in the fragile ecology of
J & K is perceived as a future environment
challange; and
(c) whether Government is satisfied
with the efforts made to protect and
conserve endangered life form particularly
Hangul, the Kashmir stag?
Allocation and utilisation of funds in
Assam
2332. SHRIMATI NAZNIN
FARUQUE: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of funds allocated and
spent in Assam by the Ministry and its
various organizations during the last three
years and the current year, so far;
(b) the details of purposes for which
these funds were given and spent; and
(c) the steps being taken to increase
allocation of these funds?

536
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Destruction of forests due to soil
erosion
†2333. SHRI MAHENDRA SINGH
MAHRA: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry is aware that
due to land erosion in hilly States, the dense
forests in the country are getting destroyed;
(b) if so, whether the Ministry would
give any suggestion to States to build check
dams in these areas to protect these dense
forests;
(c) if not, whether Ministry has any
alternative scheme to protect these dense
forests; and
(d) if so, the details thereof
